candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies → Adverse Effects/Immunotherapy: understand medication action, monitor for multisystem immune-mediated toxicity, and educate clients to report new or worsening symptoms during and after therapy.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — pembrolizumab immune-mediated adverse reactions
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that pembrolizumab's PD-1 immune activation can cause multisystem immune-mediated adverse reactions that may occur during or after treatment and therefore require ongoing symptom surveillance.

options.A: Pembrolizumab activates antitumor immune responses by blocking PD-1 signaling, but this can also produce immune-mediated inflammation or injury in normal organs and tissues, sometimes during treatment or after it ends.
options.B: Pembrolizumab suppresses the entire immune system, so these questions are mainly intended to detect ordinary opportunistic infections caused by global immunosuppression.
options.C: Pembrolizumab affects only the tumor site, so symptoms involving the lungs, bowel, liver, skin, or endocrine glands are unrelated to treatment.
options.D: Immune-mediated adverse reactions occur only during the infusion itself and cannot begin after the infusion or after treatment has been completed.

candidate.rationale: Current FDA labeling identifies pembrolizumab as a PD-1-blocking antibody. Blocking the PD-1 pathway can enhance T-cell antitumor activity but can also cause severe or fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions in essentially any organ system. The current Medication Guide warns that the immune system may attack normal organs and tissues, that more than one immune-mediated problem may occur at the same time, and that these problems may begin during treatment or after treatment has ended. Therefore, A is correct. B incorrectly describes global immune suppression, C denies multisystem toxicity, and D incorrectly limits toxicity to the infusion period.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports PD-1 immune activation as the therapeutic mechanism and the related possibility of severe multisystem immune-mediated adverse reactions during or after pembrolizumab treatment.
candidate.source_document_title: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) — Official Prescribing Information and Medication Guide
candidate.source_locator: Section 12.1, Mechanism of Action: pembrolizumab is a PD-1-blocking antibody that releases PD-1-mediated inhibition of the immune response and enhances antitumor responses. Section 5.1, Severe and Fatal Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions: immune-mediated adverse reactions can be severe or fatal, can occur in any organ system or tissue, and may occur during or after treatment. Medication Guide: KEYTRUDA may cause the immune system to attack normal organs/tissues; multiple problems can occur simultaneously and may occur after treatment ends.
